## devonthink
CRITICAL — Database package safety: DEVONthink databases are stored as packages (.dtBase2) or sparse images (.dtSparse, .dtArchive). Never modify, rename, move, or delete files inside a database package directly via the filesystem. All record and content operations must go through this MCP server or, as a fallback, via AppleScript. Direct filesystem manipulation will corrupt the database and cause irreversible data loss.

Batch operations: Use the uuids array parameter instead of sequential single-record calls for tag, update, move, trash, duplicate, replicate, and export operations. Batch mode is faster, reduces round trips, and returns a summary with succeeded/failed counts.

Avoiding duplicates: Use lookup_records (by name, URL, path, filename, or comment) before create_record to check whether a record already exists.

Content editing: Prefer update_record_content with mode append or insert over replace for large documents. Replace mode requires sending the entire new content and risks accidental data loss if the content is incomplete.

Group hierarchies: Use create_group_path to create nested group structures in a single call (like mkdir -p) rather than sequential create_record calls.

AI-powered tools: classify_record and find_similar_records use DEVONthink's built-in AI algorithms and proprietary training data — they provide organizational suggestions that complement, not duplicate, your own capabilities.

Record enrichment: resolve_doi_metadata and resolve_book_metadata can enrich existing records with bibliographic metadata by passing the record's uuid — there is no need to create a new record.

AI exclusion: Records marked as excluded from AI access (excludeFromChat) are protected in two ways. (1) Input protection: any tool that receives such a record's UUID as an argument refuses to operate on it and returns an error. (2) Output protection: result lists from tools like search_records, classify_record, find_similar_records, get_record_children, get_record_duplicates, and the link traversal tools are filt… [truncated]

1	# Spending Report Design
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-07-09
4	**Status:** ✅ Built — table + chart views, cell drill-down, hierarchy editing
5	(assign categories to groups, re-parent groups, add & rename Groupings), and
6	**historical-year expense upload from CSV/Excel** are all shipped and live.
7	Remaining work is the [Deferred](#deferred-later-slices) slices (year-over-year /
8	prior-period overlay — now unblocked by the historical upload — plus period
9	selection and export). Grouping tier editing is built; what's left of "tier CRUD"
10	is deliberately out of scope (fixed Importance areas, no Grouping delete/reorder).
11	
12	## Overview
13	
14	A top-level **Spending** report that rolls up Expenses by **Importance →
15	Grouping → Category** across the months of a year. It replaces the Excel pivot
16	table the family currently maintains by hand. ("Spending Report" is the working
17	term; pin the final ubiquitous-language name in `domain-model.md` when built.)
18	
19	Built ✅: the **table view** (v1), the **chart view** (an accordion magnitude bar
20	chart), **cell drill-down** into the Expenses view, and **hierarchy editing**
21	(assign categories to groups, re-parent groups, assign-on-create) — see
22	[Implementation status](#implementation-status),
23	[Spending Chart](#spending-chart-graphical-presentation--built-),
24	[Drill-down](#drill-from-a-table-cell-into-the-expenses-view--built-), and
25	[Editable hierarchy](#editable-hierarchy--assign--re-parent--built-). Still
26	deferred: selectable periods, year-over-year comparison, historical-year upload,
27	tier CRUD, and export (see [Deferred](#deferred-later-slices)).
28	
29	## Data model (new)
30	
31	The category hierarchy today is flat: `categories (family_id, name, color)`.
32	There is no Grouping or Importance layer. v1 adds two tiers as real,
33	family-scoped tables so they are first-class and become editable later.
34	
35	- `importance_areas (id, family_id, name, sort_order)` — e.g. Essential
36	  (sort_order 1), Priorities (2), Other (3). The numeric prefix in the sample
37	  (`1. Essential`) becomes `sort_order`, not part of the name.
38	- `category_groups (id, family_id, name, importance_area_id)` — **Importance
39	  attaches to the Grouping**, not to individual categories. Matches the sample
40	  (all of Transportation is Essential) and makes the roll-up a clean two-hop
41	  join. If a future need arises for two categories in one group to have
42	  different importances, revisit — no counterexample in the current sample.
43	- `categories` gains `group_id → category_groups`. A Category belongs to a
44	  Group; the Group carries the Importance.
45	
46	**Seeding.** Derive default Importance areas and Groupings from
47	`docs/SampleHierachy.txt` (cleaned). Map the existing default categories into
48	Groups by name. Near-duplicate categories in the sample (`Car - Insurance` vs
49	`Car insurance`, `Gas` vs `Car - Gas`, `Parking` vs `Car - Parking`) are **not
50	auto-merged** — recognizable names are mapped, the rest fall to Uncategorized.
51	New families are seeded via the same path as `createDefaultCategories`, so any
52	future family gets a working report out of the box.
53	
54	## Report content
55	
56	- **Source:** receipts/Expenses (the app's source of truth for spending), **not**
57	  bank transactions. Bucketed by `transaction_date` (purchase date, not upload
58	  date).
59	- **Currency:** normalized to the family's display currency —
60	  `total_amount × (exchange_rate_to_cad ?? 1)`. CAD for now; the assumption is
61	  isolated so multi-currency drops in later.
62	- **Columns:** January → the last month that has any expense (left edge stays at
63	  January for a stable calendar grid). Interior/empty cells render blank, not
64	  `$0.00`. Final column is labelled **"Year to Date."**
65	- **Rows:** four row types — category detail, **Grouping subtotal**,
66	  **Importance subtotal**, and a final **Grand Total**. Importance ordered by
67	  `sort_order` (Essential → Priorities → Other); Groupings alphabetical within an
68	  Importance; Categories alphabetical within a Grouping. **Zero-activity rows are
69	  suppressed** (a category/group with no spend in the visible window is hidden).
70	- **Uncategorized:** rendered as its own section at the bottom, outside the real
71	  Importance/Grouping subtotals. It **is included in the Grand Total** (and any
72	  month-column totals), so the bottom-right number ties out to the family's
73	  actual total spend. The gap between the three Importance subtotals and the
74	  Grand Total is the deliberate nudge to go categorize.
75	- **Null amounts:** counted as `$0`. No new flag — the receipts and expenses
76	  pages already badge these (`⚠ Amount not read`). At most a small "N receipts
77	  missing an amount" footnote deep-linking to that existing filtered view.
78	
79	## Architecture
80	
81	- **Client-side pure aggregation.** A tested pure function
82	  `buildSpendingReport(expenses, hierarchy, year) → grid`, in the style of the
83	  CSV parsers and date utilities. The small hierarchy tables and the year's
84	  expenses are fetched separately and joined in TypeScript — the existing
85	  expense query is not widened. A family's yearly receipt count is small, so the
86	  data transfer is negligible and the logic stays unit-testable. If volume ever
87	  demands it, swap in a Postgres RPC behind the same function boundary — this
88	  avoids the RLS-fragility minefield the codebase repeatedly warns about.
89	- **Placement:** a new top-level **`/spending`** tab, following the existing
90	  `resolve()` / `filterQuery` nav pattern. May be promoted to the home page
91	  later once proven (currently `/` is "Family Receipts") — a separate change.
92	- **No editing UI in v1.** The hierarchy is hand-maintained (direct SQL) while
93	  the family is a single maintainer. The Uncategorized bucket is the feedback
94	  loop for anything unmapped.
95	
96	## Implementation status ✅
97	
98	v1 is built and running against live data (v0.50). What landed:
99	
100	- **Migration** `supabase/migrations/20260709_spending_hierarchy.sql` — creates
101	  `importance_areas` and `category_groups`, adds `categories.group_id`
102	  (`ON DELETE SET NULL`), family-scoped RLS mirroring `categories_family_access`,
103	  unique-per-family name indexes, and `updated_at` triggers. Ships
104	  `create_default_hierarchy(p_family_id)` (idempotent, `SECURITY DEFINER`): seeds
105	  3 Importance areas + 13 Groupings and maps categories → groups by name (a
106	  superset covering both the current default names and the older spreadsheet
107	  names). Backfills every existing family in a `DO` loop; the app calls it via
108	  RPC for new families.
109	- **Grouping → Importance seed choices.** Each Grouping is collapsed to a single
110	  Importance (the model attaches Importance to the Grouping): **Essential** =
111	  Everyday, Health, Home, Transportation, Income Taxes; **Priorities** = Banking
112	  & Investing, Debt, Fitness, Kids, Rental; **Other** = Discretionary, Gifts,
113	  Travel. Where the source spreadsheet split a Grouping across importances (e.g.
114	  Home's Garden/Household goods were "Other"), it now rolls up under the
115	  Grouping's single Importance. Change with a one-row `UPDATE` on
116	  `category_groups.importance_area_id`.
117	- **Aggregation** `src/lib/utils/spendingReport.ts` — the pure
118	  `buildSpendingReport(expenses, categories, groups, importanceAreas, year)`.
119	  21 unit tests in `spendingReport.spec.ts` (month columns, roll-up/subtotals,
120	  ordering, Uncategorized, refund netting, FX, null amounts, blank-vs-zero cells).
121	  Per-cell `{ amount, count }` drives blank (count 0) vs `0.00` (net-zero but had
122	  activity).
123	- **Types** `src/lib/types/Hierarchy.ts` (`ImportanceArea`, `CategoryGroup`);
124	  `Category` gains `group_id`.
125	- **Service** `CategoryService` gains `getFamilyImportanceAreas`,
126	  `getFamilyGroups`, and `createDefaultHierarchy` (RPC wrapper).
127	- **Page + nav** `src/routes/spending/+page.svelte` + a **Spending** top-level
128	  tab. Self-seeds the hierarchy on first open (mirrors default-categories
129	  lazy-init), then loads hierarchy + the year's expenses and paints the grid.
130	  Year prev/next selector, missing-amount footnote, Importance bands, Grouping
131	  and Importance subtotals, Uncategorized section, Grand Total. The **selected
132	  year lives in the URL** (`/spending?year=2025`) and is read in a **`+page.ts`
133	  `load`** (pure `parseYearParam`); the page consumes `data.year`, and the year
134	  arrows `goto('?year=…', { replaceState: true })`. A reload `$effect` fires when
135	  `data.year` (or the resolved family) changes. `load` is the single source of
136	  truth: SvelteKit re-runs it with the correct URL on every navigation — arrows,
137	  a refresh, and **Back from a cell drill-down** — so it never snaps back to the
138	  current year (which would show an empty grid for a data-only-in-2025 family).
139	  Three client-side attempts failed first and are recorded so they aren't retried:
140	  (1) read-once-in-`onMount` raced the initial render; (2) `$derived` off the
141	  legacy `$app/stores` `$page` store went stale on Back; (3) `$derived` off the
142	  `$app/state` reactive `page` *plus* `replaceState`-driven arrows still went
143	  stale on Back and left the arrows inert. The `load` approach is the robust fix.
144	  Fix pending release (version assigned on commit).
145	- **Rendering details.** Long category names truncate to one line
146	  (`max-w-64 truncate`) with the full name on hover via `title`. The layout gives
147	  `/spending` full window width (`max-w-full`); other pages keep `max-w-5xl`.
148	
149	**Verification:** `npm run check`, `eslint`, and Prettier clean on touched files;
150	full unit suite green (1278 passed / 8 skipped, incl. the 21 new). Production
151	build succeeds. Not yet exercised: a rendered end-to-end pass (no local
152	auth/seed harness) — validated live by the maintainer instead.
153	
154	**Known open item surfaced by live data:** the seed maps by name, so any custom
155	or renamed category lands in Uncategorized until its `group_id` is set by hand.
156	
157	## Spending Chart (graphical presentation) — built ✅
158	
159	A `Table | Chart` toggle on `/spending` (shared year selector + loaded data)
160	adds a **magnitude bar chart** view (v0.60).
161	
162	> **Design note — why not stacked-by-month.** The first cut stacked 12 month
163	> segments per bar with a sequential ramp. In real data it failed twice: the 12
164	> subtle shades read as noise ("the gradient is a mess"), and one dominant
165	> Grouping (a family's ~$33k Home, driven by a one-off $20k renovation) crushed
166	> every other bar's height so small bars were unreadable. Both flaws trace to the
167	> month stack. v0.60 drops it: **solid magnitude bars + value labels**, with the
168	> month/time story deferred to the separate trend chart.
169	
170	- **Form:** one **solid bar per Grouping** = its year-to-date total, **coloured by
171	  Area of Importance** (a validated 3-colour categorical palette: Essential
172	  `#4f46e5`, Priorities `#0d9488`, Other `#d97706`; Uncategorized neutral gray).
173	  Bars ordered by Importance `sort_order` then Grouping name; **Uncategorized**
174	  trails; zero-activity groups suppressed.
175	- **Value label** above every bar (formatted currency), so a tiny bar next to a
176	  dominant one is still readable — the fix for the outlier problem without a
177	  scale hack. Positioned from the bound LayerChart `context` (band x-scale +
178	  linear y-scale).
179	- **Two bracket rows beneath the axis** carry the hierarchy, both positioned from
180	  the bound `context` band x-scale (aligned on resize):
181	  - **Row 1 — Grouping ± toggles.** One keyboard-focusable `<button>` bracket per
182	    Grouping, spanning its bar(s), showing `+ Name` / `− Name`. This is the
183	    expand/collapse control (see interaction) and the Grouping label.
184	  - **Row 2 — Area of Importance**, labelled **once per contiguous run** of
185	    same-Importance bars, in that Importance's colour. Uncategorized has no
186	    Importance bracket (its Grouping bracket names it).
187	- **Interaction: expand in place (accordion), not drill-and-replace.** Clicking a
188	  Grouping's bar **or** its ± bracket expands it into its **Category** bars _in
189	  place_ while its siblings stay visible; **any number of Groupings can be open at
190	  once** (`expandedGroups` is a reactive `SvelteSet`). Expanded Categories keep the
191	  parent Grouping's Importance colour and sit inside the same Importance bracket.
192	  Bars are keyed by a unique id, not name, so same-named Categories across
193	  Groupings don't collide on the band scale.
194	- **Click + hover come from a custom per-bar overlay, not LayerChart.** LayerChart's
195	  own tooltip layer both swallows bar clicks and can't carry a month breakdown, so
196	  `tooltipContext` is disabled and a transparent full-height column is drawn over
197	  each bar (from the band scale). It handles the click (toggle its Grouping) and the
198	  hover, which shows a **tooltip with the bar's name, its per-month totals, and the
199	  grand total** — the monthly detail dropped from the bars themselves. The overlay
200	  columns are `aria-hidden`/non-focusable mouse affordances; the ± brackets remain
201	  the keyboard-accessible controls.
202	- **Long labels don't collide.** When a Grouping expands into many Category bars,
203	  each axis label is truncated to one bar width with an ellipsis (`Meals and Drinks
204	Out` → `Meals…`); the full name is in the hover tooltip. Collapsed Grouping names
205	  live in their ± bracket (truncated there too). The one-line usage hint sits below
206	  the chart.
207	- **Data:** no new aggregation — the pure
208	  `buildSpendingChart(report, expandedGroups)` reshapes the existing
209	  `SpendingReport` into a flat `{ months, bars }` where expanded Groupings
210	  contribute their Category bars in place (unit-tested in `spendingChart.spec.ts`).
211	  The per-bar `monthly` map is retained for the future trend chart / hover detail;
212	  the current view uses only `total`.
213	- **Library:** **LayerChart 2.0.1** (`<BarChart>` with `y="total"` and a `c`
214	  ordinal colour scale by Importance; `bandPadding`, rounded bars). Peer
215	  `svelte@^5`. Its built-in tooltip/click layer (`tooltipContext`) is **disabled**
216	  in favour of the custom overlay above. Colours validated with the dataviz palette
217	  script (CVD ΔE 57.8, contrast ≥ 3:1); identity carried by position + brackets,
218	  not colour alone.
219	- **Verification:** `SpendingChart.svelte.spec.ts` (8 tests) renders it in Chromium
220	  and asserts: a bar per Grouping lays out, the once-only Importance brackets, the
221	  per-bar value labels, expand-in-place (siblings stay), several open at once,
222	  collapse back, **the bar itself (not just the bracket) expands**, and **the hover
223	  tooltip shows name + month totals + grand total**. `spendingChart.spec.ts`
224	  (6 tests) covers the pure accordion model; `spendingReport.spec.ts` (21) the
225	  aggregation.
226	
227	**Chart known limitation:**
228	
229	- **Prior-period overlay** (a line above/below the bar) is **not built** — it
230	  depends on historical-year data, which isn't loaded yet. Deferred with the
231	  upload/YoY thread below. Month-by-month detail currently lives in the Table
232	  view; a dedicated trend chart is the natural home for it.
233	
234	## Drill from a table cell into the Expenses view — built ✅
235	
236	The table's numbers are a jumping-off point (v0.55): clicking a non-blank cell
237	navigates to the **Expenses** view, filtered to exactly the Expenses that
238	produced that number.
239	
240	- **Category detail cell** (category × month) → that **category** in that
241	  **month**. **Category "Year to Date" cell** → that category across the year.
242	- **Subtotal cells** roll the filter up to match what they sum:
243	  - **Grouping subtotal** → every category id in that Grouping (that month/YTD).
244	  - **Importance subtotal** → every category id across the Importance's groups.
245	  - **Grand Total** → the date range alone (no category filter) so it ties out to
246	    all Expenses, **including Uncategorized**.
247	  - **Uncategorized** cells → the `filter=uncategorized` Expenses filter. A
248	    named-but-ungrouped category row instead drills to its own category id
249	    (precise); only the section subtotal and the "(No category)" row use the
250	    coarse `filter=uncategorized` (which by design covers only null-category
251	    Expenses, so a subtotal with ungrouped-category rows is a slight over-scope).
252	- **What shipped.**
253	  - **Pure** `buildSpendingDrilldownParams(scope, column, year, categories, groups)`
254	    → `URLSearchParams` in `src/lib/utils/spendingDrilldown.ts`; the scope
255	    (category / group / importance / uncategorized / grandTotal) and column
256	    (a month or YTD) come from the clicked row. 8 unit tests in
257	    `spendingDrilldown.spec.ts`.
258	  - **Report identity.** `buildSpendingReport` rows/sections now carry the ids the
259	    drill-down needs: `ReportRow.categoryId`, `GroupSection.id`,
260	    `ImportanceSection.id` (additive; 6 new tests, 27 total in
261	    `spendingReport.spec.ts`).
262	  - **Page.** `/spending` table cells render as `<a href>` links to `/expenses?…`;
263	    **blank cells (count 0) are not links**.
264	- **Real Expenses-page contract** (corrects the earlier guess): the params are
265	  **`dateFrom`/`dateTo`** (inclusive `YYYY-MM-DD`, via `readDateFilter`), category
266	  is **`category=id,id`**, and uncategorized is **`filter=uncategorized`** — which
267	  takes precedence over `category`, so the two are never set together.
268	- **Not yet:** the same affordance on chart bars (deferred). Verified live by the
269	  maintainer (no auth/seed harness for an end-to-end render pass), like v1.
270	
271	## Editable hierarchy — assign & re-parent — built ✅
272	
273	An **Edit hierarchy** page at **`/spending/hierarchy`** (linked from a button on
274	`/spending`) lets the maintainer restructure the hierarchy without SQL (v0.65).
275	This directly closes the "Known open item" above: custom/renamed categories that
276	the name-based seed left in Uncategorized can now be pulled into a Grouping in
277	the UI.
278	
279	- **Two mutations shipped** (the highest-value slice):
280	  - **Assign a Category to a Grouping** (or back to Uncategorized) — a per-category
281	    `<select>` grouped by Importance via `<optgroup>`.
282	    `CategoryService.assignCategoryToGroup(categoryId, groupId | null)`.
283	  - **Move a Grouping to another Area of Importance** — a per-group `<select>`.
284	    Because Importance attaches to the Grouping, this re-buckets all the group's
285	    categories at once. `CategoryService.moveGroupToImportance(groupId, importanceAreaId)`.
286	- **Unassigned bucket up top.** Categories with no `group_id` render in an amber
287	  "Unassigned categories (N)" section — the editor's whole reason to exist — each
288	  with the same group picker. Below it, the full Importance → Grouping → Category
289	  tree with **zero-activity rows NOT suppressed** (unlike the report; every group
290	  and category must be assignable).
291	- **Architecture mirrors the report.** Pure `buildHierarchyTree(importanceAreas,
292	groups, categories) → { importances, unassigned }` in
293	  `src/lib/utils/hierarchyTree.ts` shapes the three flat tables into the nested
294	  tree (Importance by `sort_order`, Groupings/Categories alphabetical; orphan
295	  groups whose Importance FK doesn't resolve fold into a trailing synthetic node
296	  so nothing is silently dropped). Presentation is a pure
297	  `HierarchyEditor.svelte` (props in, `onAssignCategory`/`onMoveGroup` out); the
298	  page owns loading + the CategoryService calls and reloads after each mutation.
299	  The page self-seeds the hierarchy if empty, like `/spending`.
300	- **Verification.** `hierarchyTree.spec.ts` (8, pure tree) +
301	  `HierarchyEditor.svelte.spec.ts` (5, renders the bucket/sections and asserts the
302	  selects emit the right ids incl. assign-to-null). `check`/eslint/Prettier clean;
303	  full suite green; production build succeeds. Live end-to-end pass by the
304	  maintainer (no auth/seed harness), like the earlier slices.
305	
306	- **Assign-on-create (v0.66).** The inline "Create new category…" form in
307	  `CategoryDropdown` (expenses page) now offers an optional **Group** selector, so
308	  a category can be filed into a Grouping at birth instead of landing in
309	  Uncategorized. `CategoryService.createCategory` gained an optional 4th `groupId`
310	  arg; the expenses page loads the family's Groupings and passes them in. The
311	  selector is hidden when no Groupings are supplied, so the receipt/reconciliation
312	  uses of `CategoryDropdown` (which don't pass `groups`) are unchanged. Tests: 3
313	  new in `CategoryDropdown.svelte.spec.ts`, 2 in `CategoryService.spec.ts`.
314	
315	- **Add & rename Groupings (v0.67).** The editor now creates new Groupings and
316	  renames existing ones, so the tier is no longer SQL-only. An **"Add a Grouping"**
317	  form (name + Area of Importance) sits below the tree
318	  (`CategoryService.createGroup(familyId, name, importanceAreaId)`); the new empty
319	  group appears in its area, ready to have categories assigned into it. Each
320	  Grouping header has an inline **Rename** (`CategoryService.renameGroup(groupId,
321	name)`) — safe because the report and editor key off the group id, not its name.
322	  Both service methods validate the name and map the unique-per-family `23505`
323	  violation to a friendly message. Tests: 4 new in `CategoryService.spec.ts`
324	  (create + rename, validation, duplicate-name), 3 in
325	  `HierarchyEditor.svelte.spec.ts` (add emits name+area, add stays disabled until
326	  both set, rename emits the edited name).
327	
328	**Out of scope — the Importance tier is fixed, permanently.** The 3 seeded areas
329	(Essential / Priorities / Other) will **not** change: there is no add/rename/
330	reorder UI and none is planned — this is a settled product decision, not a
331	deferral. Treat Importance-area CRUD as a non-goal.
332	
333	**Still deferred (Groupings):** Groupings have **no delete** — an empty Grouping
334	is inert since the report suppresses zero-activity rows, so deleting it (and the
335	delete-confirmation it would need) buys nothing. Grouping `sort_order` reorder is
336	also unbuilt (Groupings render alphabetically). Revisit only if a real need
337	appears.
338	
339	## Historical-year expense upload — built ✅
340	
341	A **Import Expenses** page at **`/expenses/import`** (buttons on both `/expenses`
342	and `/spending`) imports historical Expenses from a CSV / XLS / XLSX file
343	(pending release — version assigned on commit). This is the keystone of the
344	year-over-year thread: it's the only way to
345	get prior years' Expenses into the app so the deferred prior-period overlay /
346	YoY slices have data to compare against.
347	
348	- **File format.** Columns `Timestamp, Merchant, Amount, Category` (a `Tag`
349	  column is parsed-and-dropped — there is no tag concept in the schema). `Amount`
350	  keeps its sign: **positive = expense, negative = refund**, the same convention
351	  as `receipts.total_amount`, so refunds net against spend exactly as real
352	  receipts do (no inversion, no `abs()`). `Category` is a plain name; blank →
353	  Uncategorized.
354	- **Each row becomes an imageless receipt + a category link.** No schema change
355	  was needed: `receipts.receipt_image_path` is nullable and `createManual`
356	  already creates receipts with no image and `suspicious_date` forced `false`
357	  (these are intentional old entries). A row is one `receipts` insert plus, when
358	  it has a category, one `expense_categories` upsert (`source: 'manual'`).
359	  Category names resolve against the family's categories case-insensitively;
360	  genuinely new names are **created** and land in Uncategorized until filed in
361	  the hierarchy editor.
362	- **Two-step preview → confirm.** Unlike the transaction importer (which commits
363	  straight to the DB), this shows a preview first: how many expenses will import,
364	  how many duplicates will be skipped, which new categories will be created (with
365	  a warning + link to the hierarchy editor), and any unreadable rows. Nothing is
366	  written until the maintainer confirms.
367	- **Re-import is safe (count-based dedup).** `computeExpenseImportPlan` keys on
368	  `date | merchant | amount | category` and inserts only `max(0, fileCount −
369	dbCount)` per key, scoping the existing-rows query to the file's date range —
370	  re-running the same file is a no-op.
371	- **Architecture mirrors the report** (pure core + imperative shell). Pure:
372	  `parseExpenseImportCsv` (`src/lib/utils/expenseImportCsv.ts`),
373	  `computeExpenseImportPlan` + `buildExpenseCategoryLinks`
374	  (`src/lib/utils/expenseImportPlan.ts`). Shell: `ExpenseImportService`
375	  (`buildPreview`/`previewFromText` → `commit`). Reuse: the bank-parser CSV
376	  primitives (tokenizer, date, amount) were **extracted** from `BaseCSVParser`
377	  into `src/lib/utils/csvPrimitives.ts` (base now delegates; the 7 bank-parser
378	  suites are the oracle) so the tokenizer isn't duplicated; `ExcelToCSVConverter`
379	  handles XLS/XLSX.
380	- **Verification.** 14 tests `expenseImportCsv.spec.ts`, 12
381	  `expenseImportPlan.spec.ts`, 7 `ExpenseImportService.spec.ts` (a purpose-built
382	  Supabase fake dispatching by table/op). `check`/eslint/Prettier clean; full
383	  suite green; the 229 bank-parser tests still pass after the primitive
384	  extraction. Live end-to-end pass by the maintainer (no auth/seed harness), like
385	  the earlier slices.
386	
387	## Deferred (later slices)
388	
389	- Prior-period overlay line + year-over-year comparison (needs historical data —
390	  now **unblocked** by the historical upload above).
391	- ~~Historical-year expense upload~~ — **built ✅** (pending release), see section above.
392	- Arbitrary period / quarter selection (beyond a single calendar year).
393	- The multi-chart-type menu and any second chart type (trend, magnitude).
394	- Hierarchy tier CRUD — mostly built (assign + re-parent, and now **add/rename
395	  Groupings**, v0.67). **Importance-area CRUD is a permanent non-goal** — the 3
396	  seeded areas are fixed and will not change. Not built (but possible later):
397	  **Grouping delete** (empty groups are inert) and **Grouping reorder**
398	  (`sort_order`). See the Editable-hierarchy section above.
399	- Export (CSV / PDF).
400	- Promoting the report to the home page.
401	
402	## Known limitations (document when building)
403	
404	- **Refunds.** Refunds are represented as **negative `total_amount`** on a
405	  receipt (confirmed via `formatCurrency.spec.ts` and the export services). The
406	  report **keeps the sign**, so refunds net against spend — which is the correct
407	  behaviour for a spending total. (Note the CSV/PDF _exporters_ deliberately
408	  `abs()` refunds; the report does not.) One visible consequence: a Category or
409	  Grouping whose refunds exceed its spend in the window shows a **negative**
410	  total — informative, not a bug. No special handling needed in v1; documented
411	  here so the divergence from the exporters is intentional and searchable.
412	- **"Year to Date" label** reads oddly for a _completed past_ year (it is the
413	  full-year total). Relabel per-context when the multi-year slice lands. Not a
414	  v1 problem since v1 is current-year only.

# Spending Report Design

**Date:** 2026-07-09
**Status:** ✅ Built — table + chart views, cell drill-down, hierarchy editing
(assign categories to groups, re-parent groups, add & rename Groupings), and
**historical-year expense upload from CSV/Excel** are all shipped and live.
Remaining work is the [Deferred](#deferred-later-slices) slices (year-over-year /
prior-period overlay — now unblocked by the historical upload — plus period
selection and export). Grouping tier editing is built; what's left of "tier CRUD"
is deliberately out of scope (fixed Importance areas, no Grouping delete/reorder).

## Overview

A top-level **Spending** report that rolls up Expenses by **Importance →
Grouping → Category** across the months of a year. It replaces the Excel pivot
table the family currently maintains by hand. ("Spending Report" is the working
term; pin the final ubiquitous-language name in `domain-model.md` when built.)

Built ✅: the **table view** (v1), the **chart view** (an accordion magnitude bar
chart), **cell drill-down** into the Expenses view, and **hierarchy editing**
(assign categories to groups, re-parent groups, assign-on-create) — see
[Implementation status](#implementation-status),
[Spending Chart](#spending-chart-graphical-presentation--built-),
[Drill-down](#drill-from-a-table-cell-into-the-expenses-view--built-), and
[Editable hierarchy](#editable-hierarchy--assign--re-parent--built-). Still
deferred: selectable periods, year-over-year comparison, historical-year upload,
tier CRUD, and export (see [Deferred](#deferred-later-slices)).

## Data model (new)

The category hierarchy today is flat: `categories (family_id, name, color)`.
There is no Grouping or Importance layer. v1 adds two tiers as real,
family-scoped tables so they are first-class and become editable later.

- `importance_areas (id, family_id, name, sort_order)` — e.g. Essential
  (sort_order 1), Priorities (2), Other (3). The numeric prefix in the sample
  (`1. Essential`) becomes `sort_order`, not part of the name.
- `category_groups (id, family_id, name, importance_area_id)` — **Importance
  attaches to the Grouping**, not to individual categories. Matches the sample
  (all of Transportation is Essential) and makes the roll-up a clean two-hop
  join. If a future need arises for two categories in one group to have
  different importances, revisit — no counterexample in the current sample.
- `categories` gains `group_id → category_groups`. A Category belongs to a
  Group; the Group carries the Importance.

**Seeding.** Derive default Importance areas and Groupings from
`docs/SampleHierachy.txt` (cleaned). Map the existing default categories into
Groups by name. Near-duplicate categories in the sample (`Car - Insurance` vs
`Car insurance`, `Gas` vs `Car - Gas`, `Parking` vs `Car - Parking`) are **not
auto-merged** — recognizable names are mapped, the rest fall to Uncategorized.
New families are seeded via the same path as `createDefaultCategories`, so any
future family gets a working report out of the box.

## Report content

- **Source:** receipts/Expenses (the app's source of truth for spending), **not**
  bank transactions. Bucketed by `transaction_date` (purchase date, not upload
  date).
- **Currency:** normalized to the family's display currency —
  `total_amount × (exchange_rate_to_cad ?? 1)`. CAD for now; the assumption is
  isolated so multi-currency drops in later.
- **Columns:** January → the last month that has any expense (left edge stays at
  January for a stable calendar grid). Interior/empty cells render blank, not
  `$0.00`. Final column is labelled **"Year to Date."**
- **Rows:** four row types — category detail, **Grouping subtotal**,
  **Importance subtotal**, and a final **Grand Total**. Importance ordered by
  `sort_order` (Essential → Priorities → Other); Groupings alphabetical within an
  Importance; Categories alphabetical within a Grouping. **Zero-activity rows are
  suppressed** (a category/group with no spend in the visible window is hidden).
- **Uncategorized:** rendered as its own section at the bottom, outside the real
  Importance/Grouping subtotals. It **is included in the Grand Total** (and any
  month-column totals), so the bottom-right number ties out to the family's
  actual total spend. The gap between the three Importance subtotals and the
  Grand Total is the deliberate nudge to go categorize.
- **Null amounts:** counted as `$0`. No new flag — the receipts and expenses
  pages already badge these (`⚠ Amount not read`). At most a small "N receipts
  missing an amount" footnote deep-linking to that existing filtered view.

## Architecture

- **Client-side pure aggregation.** A tested pure function
  `buildSpendingReport(expenses, hierarchy, year) → grid`, in the style of the
  CSV parsers and date utilities. The small hierarchy tables and the year's
  expenses are fetched separately and joined in TypeScript — the existing
  expense query is not widened. A family's yearly receipt count is small, so the
  data transfer is negligible and the logic stays unit-testable. If volume ever
  demands it, swap in a Postgres RPC behind the same function boundary — this
  avoids the RLS-fragility minefield the codebase repeatedly warns about.
- **Placement:** a new top-level **`/spending`** tab, following the existing
  `resolve()` / `filterQuery` nav pattern. May be promoted to the home page
  later once proven (currently `/` is "Family Receipts") — a separate change.
- **No editing UI in v1.** The hierarchy is hand-maintained (direct SQL) while
  the family is a single maintainer. The Uncategorized bucket is the feedback
  loop for anything unmapped.

## Implementation status ✅

v1 is built and running against live data (v0.50). What landed:

- **Migration** `supabase/migrations/20260709_spending_hierarchy.sql` — creates
  `importance_areas` and `category_groups`, adds `categories.group_id`
  (`ON DELETE SET NULL`), family-scoped RLS mirroring `categories_family_access`,
  unique-per-family name indexes, and `updated_at` triggers. Ships
  `create_default_hierarchy(p_family_id)` (idempotent, `SECURITY DEFINER`): seeds
  3 Importance areas + 13 Groupings and maps categories → groups by name (a
  superset covering both the current default names and the older spreadsheet
  names). Backfills every existing family in a `DO` loop; the app calls it via
  RPC for new families.
- **Grouping → Importance seed choices.** Each Grouping is collapsed to a single
  Importance (the model attaches Importance to the Grouping): **Essential** =
  Everyday, Health, Home, Transportation, Income Taxes; **Priorities** = Banking
  & Investing, Debt, Fitness, Kids, Rental; **Other** = Discretionary, Gifts,
  Travel. Where the source spreadsheet split a Grouping across importances (e.g.
  Home's Garden/Household goods were "Other"), it now rolls up under the
  Grouping's single Importance. Change with a one-row `UPDATE` on
  `category_groups.importance_area_id`.
- **Aggregation** `src/lib/utils/spendingReport.ts` — the pure
  `buildSpendingReport(expenses, categories, groups, importanceAreas, year)`.
  21 unit tests in `spendingReport.spec.ts` (month columns, roll-up/subtotals,
  ordering, Uncategorized, refund netting, FX, null amounts, blank-vs-zero cells).
  Per-cell `{ amount, count }` drives blank (count 0) vs `0.00` (net-zero but had
  activity).
- **Types** `src/lib/types/Hierarchy.ts` (`ImportanceArea`, `CategoryGroup`);
  `Category` gains `group_id`.
- **Service** `CategoryService` gains `getFamilyImportanceAreas`,
  `getFamilyGroups`, and `createDefaultHierarchy` (RPC wrapper).
- **Page + nav** `src/routes/spending/+page.svelte` + a **Spending** top-level
  tab. Self-seeds the hierarchy on first open (mirrors default-categories
  lazy-init), then loads hierarchy + the year's expenses and paints the grid.
  Year prev/next selector, missing-amount footnote, Importance bands, Grouping
  and Importance subtotals, Uncategorized section, Grand Total. The **selected
  year lives in the URL** (`/spending?year=2025`) and is read in a **`+page.ts`
  `load`** (pure `parseYearParam`); the page consumes `data.year`, and the year
  arrows `goto('?year=…', { replaceState: true })`. A reload `$effect` fires when
  `data.year` (or the resolved family) changes. `load` is the single source of
  truth: SvelteKit re-runs it with the correct URL on every navigation — arrows,
  a refresh, and **Back from a cell drill-down** — so it never snaps back to the
  current year (which would show an empty grid for a data-only-in-2025 family).
  Three client-side attempts failed first and are recorded so they aren't retried:
  (1) read-once-in-`onMount` raced the initial render; (2) `$derived` off the
  legacy `$app/stores` `$page` store went stale on Back; (3) `$derived` off the
  `$app/state` reactive `page` *plus* `replaceState`-driven arrows still went
  stale on Back and left the arrows inert. The `load` approach is the robust fix.
  Fix pending release (version assigned on commit).
- **Rendering details.** Long category names truncate to one line
  (`max-w-64 truncate`) with the full name on hover via `title`. The layout gives
  `/spending` full window width (`max-w-full`); other pages keep `max-w-5xl`.

**Verification:** `npm run check`, `eslint`, and Prettier clean on touched files;
full unit suite green (1278 passed / 8 skipped, incl. the 21 new). Production
build succeeds. Not yet exercised: a rendered end-to-end pass (no local
auth/seed harness) — validated live by the maintainer instead.

**Known open item surfaced by live data:** the seed maps by name, so any custom
or renamed category lands in Uncategorized until its `group_id` is set by hand.

## Spending Chart (graphical presentation) — built ✅

A `Table | Chart` toggle on `/spending` (shared year selector + loaded data)
adds a **magnitude bar chart** view (v0.60).

> **Design note — why not stacked-by-month.** The first cut stacked 12 month
> segments per bar with a sequential ramp. In real data it failed twice: the 12
> subtle shades read as noise ("the gradient is a mess"), and one dominant
> Grouping (a family's ~$33k Home, driven by a one-off $20k renovation) crushed
> every other bar's height so small bars were unreadable. Both flaws trace to the
> month stack. v0.60 drops it: **solid magnitude bars + value labels**, with the
> month/time story deferred to the separate trend chart.

- **Form:** one **solid bar per Grouping** = its year-to-date total, **coloured by
  Area of Importance** (a validated 3-colour categorical palette: Essential
  `#4f46e5`, Priorities `#0d9488`, Other `#d97706`; Uncategorized neutral gray).
  Bars ordered by Importance `sort_order` then Grouping name; **Uncategorized**
  trails; zero-activity groups suppressed.
- **Value label** above every bar (formatted currency), so a tiny bar next to a
  dominant one is still readable — the fix for the outlier problem without a
  scale hack. Positioned from the bound LayerChart `context` (band x-scale +
  linear y-scale).
- **Two bracket rows beneath the axis** carry the hierarchy, both positioned from
  the bound `context` band x-scale (aligned on resize):
  - **Row 1 — Grouping ± toggles.** One keyboard-focusable `<button>` bracket per
    Grouping, spanning its bar(s), showing `+ Name` / `− Name`. This is the
    expand/collapse control (see interaction) and the Grouping label.
  - **Row 2 — Area of Importance**, labelled **once per contiguous run** of
    same-Importance bars, in that Importance's colour. Uncategorized has no
    Importance bracket (its Grouping bracket names it).
- **Interaction: expand in place (accordion), not drill-and-replace.** Clicking a
  Grouping's bar **or** its ± bracket expands it into its **Category** bars _in
  place_ while its siblings stay visible; **any number of Groupings can be open at
  once** (`expandedGroups` is a reactive `SvelteSet`). Expanded Categories keep the
  parent Grouping's Importance colour and sit inside the same Importance bracket.
  Bars are keyed by a unique id, not name, so same-named Categories across
  Groupings don't collide on the band scale.
- **Click + hover come from a custom per-bar overlay, not LayerChart.** LayerChart's
  own tooltip layer both swallows bar clicks and can't carry a month breakdown, so
  `tooltipContext` is disabled and a transparent full-height column is drawn over
  each bar (from the band scale). It handles the click (toggle its Grouping) and the
  hover, which shows a **tooltip with the bar's name, its per-month totals, and the
  grand total** — the monthly detail dropped from the bars themselves. The overlay
  columns are `aria-hidden`/non-focusable mouse affordances; the ± brackets remain
  the keyboard-accessible controls.
- **Long labels don't collide.** When a Grouping expands into many Category bars,
  each axis label is truncated to one bar width with an ellipsis (`Meals and Drinks
Out` → `Meals…`); the full name is in the hover tooltip. Collapsed Grouping names
  live in their ± bracket (truncated there too). The one-line usage hint sits below
  the chart.
- **Data:** no new aggregation — the pure
  `buildSpendingChart(report, expandedGroups)` reshapes the existing
  `SpendingReport` into a flat `{ months, bars }` where expanded Groupings
  contribute their Category bars in place (unit-tested in `spendingChart.spec.ts`).
  The per-bar `monthly` map is retained for the future trend chart / hover detail;
  the current view uses only `total`.
- **Library:** **LayerChart 2.0.1** (`<BarChart>` with `y="total"` and a `c`
  ordinal colour scale by Importance; `bandPadding`, rounded bars). Peer
  `svelte@^5`. Its built-in tooltip/click layer (`tooltipContext`) is **disabled**
  in favour of the custom overlay above. Colours validated with the dataviz palette
  script (CVD ΔE 57.8, contrast ≥ 3:1); identity carried by position + brackets,
  not colour alone.
- **Verification:** `SpendingChart.svelte.spec.ts` (8 tests) renders it in Chromium
  and asserts: a bar per Grouping lays out, the once-only Importance brackets, the
  per-bar value labels, expand-in-place (siblings stay), several open at once,
  collapse back, **the bar itself (not just the bracket) expands**, and **the hover
  tooltip shows name + month totals + grand total**. `spendingChart.spec.ts`
  (6 tests) covers the pure accordion model; `spendingReport.spec.ts` (21) the
  aggregation.

**Chart known limitation:**

- **Prior-period overlay** (a line above/below the bar) is **not built** — it
  depends on historical-year data, which isn't loaded yet. Deferred with the
  upload/YoY thread below. Month-by-month detail currently lives in the Table
  view; a dedicated trend chart is the natural home for it.

## Drill from a table cell into the Expenses view — built ✅

The table's numbers are a jumping-off point (v0.55): clicking a non-blank cell
navigates to the **Expenses** view, filtered to exactly the Expenses that
produced that number.

- **Category detail cell** (category × month) → that **category** in that
  **month**. **Category "Year to Date" cell** → that category across the year.
- **Subtotal cells** roll the filter up to match what they sum:
  - **Grouping subtotal** → every category id in that Grouping (that month/YTD).
  - **Importance subtotal** → every category id across the Importance's groups.
  - **Grand Total** → the date range alone (no category filter) so it ties out to
    all Expenses, **including Uncategorized**.
  - **Uncategorized** cells → the `filter=uncategorized` Expenses filter. A
    named-but-ungrouped category row instead drills to its own category id
    (precise); only the section subtotal and the "(No category)" row use the
    coarse `filter=uncategorized` (which by design covers only null-category
    Expenses, so a subtotal with ungrouped-category rows is a slight over-scope).
- **What shipped.**
  - **Pure** `buildSpendingDrilldownParams(scope, column, year, categories, groups)`
    → `URLSearchParams` in `src/lib/utils/spendingDrilldown.ts`; the scope
    (category / group / importance / uncategorized / grandTotal) and column
    (a month or YTD) come from the clicked row. 8 unit tests in
    `spendingDrilldown.spec.ts`.
  - **Report identity.** `buildSpendingReport` rows/sections now carry the ids the
    drill-down needs: `ReportRow.categoryId`, `GroupSection.id`,
    `ImportanceSection.id` (additive; 6 new tests, 27 total in
    `spendingReport.spec.ts`).
  - **Page.** `/spending` table cells render as `<a href>` links to `/expenses?…`;
    **blank cells (count 0) are not links**.
- **Real Expenses-page contract** (corrects the earlier guess): the params are
  **`dateFrom`/`dateTo`** (inclusive `YYYY-MM-DD`, via `readDateFilter`), category
  is **`category=id,id`**, and uncategorized is **`filter=uncategorized`** — which
  takes precedence over `category`, so the two are never set together.
- **Not yet:** the same affordance on chart bars (deferred). Verified live by the
  maintainer (no auth/seed harness for an end-to-end render pass), like v1.

## Editable hierarchy — assign & re-parent — built ✅

An **Edit hierarchy** page at **`/spending/hierarchy`** (linked from a button on
`/spending`) lets the maintainer restructure the hierarchy without SQL (v0.65).
This directly closes the "Known open item" above: custom/renamed categories that
the name-based seed left in Uncategorized can now be pulled into a Grouping in
the UI.

- **Two mutations shipped** (the highest-value slice):
  - **Assign a Category to a Grouping** (or back to Uncategorized) — a per-category
    `<select>` grouped by Importance via `<optgroup>`.
    `CategoryService.assignCategoryToGroup(categoryId, groupId | null)`.
  - **Move a Grouping to another Area of Importance** — a per-group `<select>`.
    Because Importance attaches to the Grouping, this re-buckets all the group's
    categories at once. `CategoryService.moveGroupToImportance(groupId, importanceAreaId)`.
- **Unassigned bucket up top.** Categories with no `group_id` render in an amber
  "Unassigned categories (N)" section — the editor's whole reason to exist — each
  with the same group picker. Below it, the full Importance → Grouping → Category
  tree with **zero-activity rows NOT suppressed** (unlike the report; every group
  and category must be assignable).
- **Architecture mirrors the report.** Pure `buildHierarchyTree(importanceAreas,
groups, categories) → { importances, unassigned }` in
  `src/lib/utils/hierarchyTree.ts` shapes the three flat tables into the nested
  tree (Importance by `sort_order`, Groupings/Categories alphabetical; orphan
  groups whose Importance FK doesn't resolve fold into a trailing synthetic node
  so nothing is silently dropped). Presentation is a pure
  `HierarchyEditor.svelte` (props in, `onAssignCategory`/`onMoveGroup` out); the
  page owns loading + the CategoryService calls and reloads after each mutation.
  The page self-seeds the hierarchy if empty, like `/spending`.
- **Verification.** `hierarchyTree.spec.ts` (8, pure tree) +
  `HierarchyEditor.svelte.spec.ts` (5, renders the bucket/sections and asserts the
  selects emit the right ids incl. assign-to-null). `check`/eslint/Prettier clean;
  full suite green; production build succeeds. Live end-to-end pass by the
  maintainer (no auth/seed harness), like the earlier slices.

- **Assign-on-create (v0.66).** The inline "Create new category…" form in
  `CategoryDropdown` (expenses page) now offers an optional **Group** selector, so
  a category can be filed into a Grouping at birth instead of landing in
  Uncategorized. `CategoryService.createCategory` gained an optional 4th `groupId`
  arg; the expenses page loads the family's Groupings and passes them in. The
  selector is hidden when no Groupings are supplied, so the receipt/reconciliation
  uses of `CategoryDropdown` (which don't pass `groups`) are unchanged. Tests: 3
  new in `CategoryDropdown.svelte.spec.ts`, 2 in `CategoryService.spec.ts`.

- **Add & rename Groupings (v0.67).** The editor now creates new Groupings and
  renames existing ones, so the tier is no longer SQL-only. An **"Add a Grouping"**
  form (name + Area of Importance) sits below the tree
  (`CategoryService.createGroup(familyId, name, importanceAreaId)`); the new empty
  group appears in its area, ready to have categories assigned into it. Each
  Grouping header has an inline **Rename** (`CategoryService.renameGroup(groupId,
name)`) — safe because the report and editor key off the group id, not its name.
  Both service methods validate the name and map the unique-per-family `23505`
  violation to a friendly message. Tests: 4 new in `CategoryService.spec.ts`
  (create + rename, validation, duplicate-name), 3 in
  `HierarchyEditor.svelte.spec.ts` (add emits name+area, add stays disabled until
  both set, rename emits the edited name).

**Out of scope — the Importance tier is fixed, permanently.** The 3 seeded areas
(Essential / Priorities / Other) will **not** change: there is no add/rename/
reorder UI and none is planned — this is a settled product decision, not a
deferral. Treat Importance-area CRUD as a non-goal.

**Still deferred (Groupings):** Groupings have **no delete** — an empty Grouping
is inert since the report suppresses zero-activity rows, so deleting it (and the
delete-confirmation it would need) buys nothing. Grouping `sort_order` reorder is
also unbuilt (Groupings render alphabetically). Revisit only if a real need
appears.

## Historical-year expense upload — built ✅

A **Import Expenses** page at **`/expenses/import`** (buttons on both `/expenses`
and `/spending`) imports historical Expenses from a CSV / XLS / XLSX file
(pending release — version assigned on commit). This is the keystone of the
year-over-year thread: it's the only way to
get prior years' Expenses into the app so the deferred prior-period overlay /
YoY slices have data to compare against.

- **File format.** Columns `Timestamp, Merchant, Amount, Category` (a `Tag`
  column is parsed-and-dropped — there is no tag concept in the schema). `Amount`
  keeps its sign: **positive = expense, negative = refund**, the same convention
  as `receipts.total_amount`, so refunds net against spend exactly as real
  receipts do (no inversion, no `abs()`). `Category` is a plain name; blank →
  Uncategorized.
- **Each row becomes an imageless receipt + a category link.** No schema change
  was needed: `receipts.receipt_image_path` is nullable and `createManual`
  already creates receipts with no image and `suspicious_date` forced `false`
  (these are intentional old entries). A row is one `receipts` insert plus, when
  it has a category, one `expense_categories` upsert (`source: 'manual'`).
  Category names resolve against the family's categories case-insensitively;
  genuinely new names are **created** and land in Uncategorized until filed in
  the hierarchy editor.
- **Two-step preview → confirm.** Unlike the transaction importer (which commits
  straight to the DB), this shows a preview first: how many expenses will import,
  how many duplicates will be skipped, which new categories will be created (with
  a warning + link to the hierarchy editor), and any unreadable rows. Nothing is
  written until the maintainer confirms.
- **Re-import is safe (count-based dedup).** `computeExpenseImportPlan` keys on
  `date | merchant | amount | category` and inserts only `max(0, fileCount −
dbCount)` per key, scoping the existing-rows query to the file's date range —
  re-running the same file is a no-op.
- **Architecture mirrors the report** (pure core + imperative shell). Pure:
  `parseExpenseImportCsv` (`src/lib/utils/expenseImportCsv.ts`),
  `computeExpenseImportPlan` + `buildExpenseCategoryLinks`
  (`src/lib/utils/expenseImportPlan.ts`). Shell: `ExpenseImportService`
  (`buildPreview`/`previewFromText` → `commit`). Reuse: the bank-parser CSV
  primitives (tokenizer, date, amount) were **extracted** from `BaseCSVParser`
  into `src/lib/utils/csvPrimitives.ts` (base now delegates; the 7 bank-parser
  suites are the oracle) so the tokenizer isn't duplicated; `ExcelToCSVConverter`
  handles XLS/XLSX.
- **Verification.** 14 tests `expenseImportCsv.spec.ts`, 12
  `expenseImportPlan.spec.ts`, 7 `ExpenseImportService.spec.ts` (a purpose-built
  Supabase fake dispatching by table/op). `check`/eslint/Prettier clean; full
  suite green; the 229 bank-parser tests still pass after the primitive
  extraction. Live end-to-end pass by the maintainer (no auth/seed harness), like
  the earlier slices.

## Deferred (later slices)

- Prior-period overlay line + year-over-year comparison (needs historical data —
  now **unblocked** by the historical upload above).
- ~~Historical-year expense upload~~ — **built ✅** (pending release), see section above.
- Arbitrary period / quarter selection (beyond a single calendar year).
- The multi-chart-type menu and any second chart type (trend, magnitude).
- Hierarchy tier CRUD — mostly built (assign + re-parent, and now **add/rename
  Groupings**, v0.67). **Importance-area CRUD is a permanent non-goal** — the 3
  seeded areas are fixed and will not change. Not built (but possible later):
  **Grouping delete** (empty groups are inert) and **Grouping reorder**
  (`sort_order`). See the Editable-hierarchy section above.
- Export (CSV / PDF).
- Promoting the report to the home page.

## Known limitations (document when building)

- **Refunds.** Refunds are represented as **negative `total_amount`** on a
  receipt (confirmed via `formatCurrency.spec.ts` and the export services). The
  report **keeps the sign**, so refunds net against spend — which is the correct
  behaviour for a spending total. (Note the CSV/PDF _exporters_ deliberately
  `abs()` refunds; the report does not.) One visible consequence: a Category or
  Grouping whose refunds exceed its spend in the window shows a **negative**
  total — informative, not a bug. No special handling needed in v1; documented
  here so the divergence from the exporters is intentional and searchable.
- **"Year to Date" label** reads oddly for a _completed past_ year (it is the
  full-year total). Relabel per-context when the multi-year slice lands. Not a
  v1 problem since v1 is current-year only.

This is a design question that builds directly on the doc's deferred "prior-period overlay / YoY" thread. Let me lay out the options, then recommend a combination — and nail down the parity rule since that's the load-bearing constraint.

## The parity rule first (it governs every option)

Everything below depends on one shared primitive: a **"period cutoff"** derived from the current year's data, applied identically to every comparison year.

- Cutoff = the last month with any current-year expense (the doc already computes this for the table's rightmost column — reuse it, don't invent a second rule).
- Every comparison year is summed **Jan → cutoff month only**. Prior-year Aug–Dec is excluded from the headline comparison so a partial 2026 never loses to a full 2025 by construction.
- **Edge to decide: month vs. day granularity.** Today is 2026-07-10, so July is partial in 2026 but was complete in 2025. A strict pace comparison would cap both at Jan 1–Jul 10; the simpler month-boundary version compares Jan–Jul wholesale (mildly unfair in the current partial month). Recommendation: **month-boundary for the table/bar overlays** (matches the monthly grid, easy to explain), and **day-boundary only for the cumulative pace line** where the whole point is "are we ahead of last year *right now*." Label the truncation explicitly wherever it applies — the doc's own "Year to Date" note (L412) already flags that a full past year mislabels.

## Options, roughly cheapest → richest

**1. YoY columns in the existing table (cheapest, highest certainty).**
Add two columns after "Year to Date": **"Prior YTD"** (same Jan→cutoff period, prior year) and **"Δ %"** (or absolute Δ). Same roll-up levels as today (category / group / importance / grand total). Zero new chart infra — pure extension of `buildSpendingReport`, and it drills the same way. This is the safe backbone; ship it regardless of which chart you pick.

**2. Prior-period marker on the magnitude bar chart (the doc's stated deferred item, L228–231).**
Per Grouping bar (current YTD), draw a **horizontal tick / ghost bar** at the prior-YTD value. The gap between bar top and tick *is* the change, read at a glance, in place, with the accordion still working. Small, in the view people already use.

**3. Cumulative "pace" line chart — my top pick for "how has spending changed."**
X = month (Jan → cutoff), Y = **running cumulative spend**, **one line per year** overlaid. Current year's line simply stops at the cutoff month; prior years are drawn only to the same X so the lines are directly comparable and the parity rule is *visually self-evident* (all lines end at the same x). Answers "are we spending faster or slower than last year?" better than anything else, and it's the natural home for the month/time story the doc deliberately deferred off the bars (L168, L232). Start at Grand Total; let a Grouping selector swap the series.

**4. Diverging change bars — best for "*what* changed."**
One bar per Grouping = **Δ vs prior YTD**, increases one direction, decreases the other, sorted by magnitude. Instantly surfaces "Travel up $2k, Groceries down $400." **Color caution:** the app already binds red = expense / green = refund (CLAUDE.md, and the chart's Importance palette). Don't overload red/green here — use a neutral diverging pair (or keep Importance colors and encode direction by side + sign label) so "spent more" isn't misread as "refund."

**5. Waterfall / bridge (richest single-story view).**
Start bar = prior-YTD grand total, one step per Grouping's ±Δ, end bar = current-YTD total. Decomposes the *entire* year-over-year change into contributors. Powerful but the most new chart code and the least reuse of existing infra — a later slice, not the first.

**Deliberately skipping:** month×grouping heatmaps and indexed-to-100 growth curves — both are legible only to spreadsheet-native users and this report exists to *replace* the family's manual pivot, not re-create its density.

## Recommendation

Sequence them so each slice stands alone:

1. **YoY table columns** (#1) — backbone, drills already, near-zero risk.
2. **Prior-period marker on the bars** (#2) — the doc's already-scoped deferred item, in the view users know.
3. **Cumulative pace line** (#3) as the dedicated trend chart the doc keeps pointing at.
4. Diverging change bars (#4) / waterfall (#5) later if the family wants "what/why decomposed."

All four consume the **same** parity-truncated aggregate — extend `buildSpendingReport` to emit `{ current, priorPeriod }` per cell/row (Jan→cutoff both years) once, and every visualization above reads from it. That keeps the pure-core/tested-aggregate discipline the doc already follows (L81–88).

Want me to write this up as a new **"Year-over-year visualization"** section in the design doc (replacing/expanding the one-liner at L389), with the parity rule and the recommended slice order? I'd keep it in the deferred-but-now-planned voice the rest of the doc uses.

## Year-over-year comparison — table columns & bar marker built ✅

Now that historical years can be uploaded, the report can show **how spending
changed vs. prior years**. This section catalogues the visualization options,
then records what shipped first.

### The parity rule (load-bearing — governs every option)

Every comparison shares one primitive: a **period cutoff** derived from the
selected year's own data, applied identically to each comparison year.

- **Cutoff = the selected year's last visible month** — the same `maxMonth` the
  report already computes for the rightmost ("Year to Date") column. Reused, not
  re-derived.
- Each comparison year is summed **January → cutoff month only**. A partial 2026
  (Jan–Jul) is compared against **Jan–Jul** of the prior year, never its full
  Jan–Dec — so a half-finished current year can't lose by construction.
- **Whole months only** (the shipped choice). Today being 2026-07-10, July is
  partial in 2026 but was complete in 2025; the month-boundary rule compares
  Jan–Jul wholesale rather than clipping both to Jul 10. Simpler, matches the
  monthly grid, and is what the maintainer asked to start with. A day-boundary
  "pace" comparison is possible later (see the cumulative line below) but is not
  built.

### The options (cheapest → richest)

1. **YoY table columns** — after "Year to Date", a **Prior-YTD** column (same
   Jan→cutoff period, prior year) and a **Change** column (Δ amount + %). Same
   roll-up levels as today (category / group / importance / grand total). Pure
   extension of the aggregate; no new chart infra. **Built (below).**
2. **Prior-period marker on the magnitude bars** — a horizontal tick / ghost line
   at each bar's prior-YTD value; the gap between bar top and tick *is* the
   change, read in place with the accordion still working. **Built (below).**
3. **Cumulative "pace" line chart** — x = month (Jan → cutoff), y = running
   cumulative spend, **one line per year** overlaid, every line stopping at the
   same cutoff x so the parity rule is visually self-evident. The natural home
   for the month/time story deliberately dropped off the bars. **Deferred.**
4. **Diverging change bars** — one bar per Grouping = Δ vs prior YTD, increases
   one way / decreases the other, sorted by magnitude; best for *what* changed.
   **Deferred.** (Colour caution: the app already binds red = expense /
   green = refund, so a diverging chart must not reuse red/green for
   direction — use a neutral diverging pair or encode direction by side + sign.)
5. **Waterfall / bridge** — prior-YTD total → one ±step per Grouping →
   current-YTD total; decomposes the entire YoY change. Richest, least reuse.
   **Deferred.**

Deliberately skipped: month×grouping heatmaps and indexed-to-100 growth curves —
legible only to spreadsheet-native users, and this report exists to *replace* the
family's manual pivot, not re-create its density.

### What shipped (options 1 + 2, pending release)

- **Toggle.** A **`Compare {priorYear}`** button in the header (next to
  Table | Chart) turns the comparison on/off for **both** views. When the prior
  year has **no data**, the toggle still renders but is **disabled** with an
  explanatory `title` ("No {priorYear} data to compare"). Effective state is
  `comparing = compare && hasPrior`, so stepping the year selector onto a year
  whose predecessor has no data silently disables it and re-enables on return.
  Comparison is **local page state** (like the Table | Chart toggle), not URL —
  it doesn't affect drill-down navigation, so it needn't survive Back.
- **Pure core.** `withPriorPeriod(report, priorReport)` in
  `src/lib/utils/spendingComparison.ts` attaches `priorYtd` (optional field added
  to `ReportRow`) to every row/subtotal/grand-total by summing the prior report's
  cells over the first `report.months.length` months (the parity window), matched
  by **id** (categoryId / groupId / importanceId) with `(No category)` matched by
  name. `spendingChange(current, prior) → { delta, pct, direction }` computes the
  Change cell (pct is `null` when prior is 0 → rendered "new"); `hasPriorData`

## Year-over-year comparison — table columns & bar marker built ✅

Now that historical years can be uploaded, the report can show **how spending
changed vs. prior years**. This section catalogues the visualization options,
then records what shipped first.

### The parity rule (load-bearing — governs every option)

Every comparison shares one primitive: a **period cutoff** derived from the
selected year's own data, applied identically to each comparison year.

- **Cutoff = the selected year's last visible month** — the same `maxMonth` the
  report already computes for the rightmost ("Year to Date") column. Reused, not
  re-derived.
- Each comparison year is summed **January → cutoff month only**. A partial 2026
  (Jan–Jul) is compared against **Jan–Jul** of the prior year, never its full
  Jan–Dec — so a half-finished current year can't lose by construction.
- **Whole months only** (the shipped choice). Today being 2026-07-10, July is
  partial in 2026 but was complete in 2025; the month-boundary rule compares
  Jan–Jul wholesale rather than clipping both to Jul 10. Simpler, matches the
  monthly grid, and is what the maintainer asked to start with. A day-boundary
  "pace" comparison is possible later (see the cumulative line below) but is not
  built.

### The options (cheapest → richest)

1. **YoY table columns** — after "Year to Date", a **Prior-YTD** column (same
   Jan→cutoff period, prior year) and a **Change** column (Δ amount + %). Same
   roll-up levels as today (category / group / importance / grand total). Pure
   extension of the aggregate; no new chart infra. **Built (below).**
2. **Prior-period marker on the magnitude bars** — a horizontal tick / ghost line
   at each bar's prior-YTD value; the gap between bar top and tick *is* the
   change, read in place with the accordion still working. **Built (below).**
3. **Cumulative "pace" line chart** — x = month (Jan → cutoff), y = running
   cumulative spend, **one line per year** overlaid, every line stopping at the
   same cutoff x so the parity rule is visually self-evident. The natural home
   for the month/time story deliberately dropped off the bars. **Deferred.**
4. **Diverging change bars** — one bar per Grouping = Δ vs prior YTD, increases
   one way / decreases the other, sorted by magnitude; best for *what* changed.
   **Deferred.** (Colour caution: the app already binds red = expense /
   green = refund, so a diverging chart must not reuse red/green for
   direction — use a neutral diverging pair or encode direction by side + sign.)
5. **Waterfall / bridge** — prior-YTD total → one ±step per Grouping →
   current-YTD total; decomposes the entire YoY change. Richest, least reuse.
   **Deferred.**

Deliberately skipped: month×grouping heatmaps and indexed-to-100 growth curves —
legible only to spreadsheet-native users, and this report exists to *replace* the
family's manual pivot, not re-create its density.

### What shipped (options 1 + 2, pending release)

- **Toggle.** A **`Compare {priorYear}`** button in the header (next to
  Table | Chart) turns the comparison on/off for **both** views. When the prior
  year has **no data**, the toggle still renders but is **disabled** with an
  explanatory `title` ("No {priorYear} data to compare"). Effective state is
  `comparing = compare && hasPrior`, so stepping the year selector onto a year
  whose predecessor has no data silently disables it and re-enables on return.
  Comparison is **local page state** (like the Table | Chart toggle), not URL —
  it doesn't affect drill-down navigation, so it needn't survive Back.
- **Pure core.** `withPriorPeriod(report, priorReport)` in
  `src/lib/utils/spendingComparison.ts` attaches `priorYtd` (optional field added
  to `ReportRow`) to every row/subtotal/grand-total by summing the prior report's
  cells over the first `report.months.length` months (the parity window), matched

  name. `spendingChange(current, prior) → { delta, pct, direction }` computes the

  more / green = spent less / grey = flat** with a signed amount and %. The
  Importance/Uncategorized band `colspan`s widen by 2 when comparing.
- **Chart.** `buildSpendingChart` carries `priorTotal` onto each `ChartBar`

  a dashed prior-period line across each bar from the bound y-scale, and adds the
  prior total + change to the hover tooltip. Data loading fetches the prior year's
  expenses alongside the current year's (volume is negligible per the aggregate's
  own design note), so switching the toggle repaints instantly with no refetch.

**Known limitations (documented, not bugs).**

- **Disappeared spend is invisible here.** Columns and markers hang off the
  *current* report's rows, so a Grouping/Category that had spend last year but
  none this year has no row to annotate. Surfacing vanished spend needs the
  diverging or waterfall view (deferred). The Grand-Total row still reflects it.
- **Marker overflow.** If a bar's prior-period total exceeds the tallest current
  bar (spending in that group dropped sharply), its dashed line sits above the
  plot area. Rare for same-period comparisons; the tooltip always carries the
  exact number. Revisit if it bites.
- **Whole-month only** (see the parity rule) — the current partial month is
  compared against the prior year's *full* same month.

All green — full suite: **1424 passed / 8 skipped**. Here's what I did.

## Design doc
Added a **"Year-over-year comparison"** section to `docs/plans/2026-07-09-spending-report-design.md` that writes up all five visualization options (YoY columns → bar marker → cumulative pace line → diverging change bars → waterfall), the **parity rule** that governs them (cutoff = the selected year's last visible month, applied identically to the prior year; whole-months-only as you asked), and marks options **1 & 2 as built**. I also threaded the status through the header, overview, chart-limitation, and deferred lists.

## Implemented (options 1 & 2)
- **`src/lib/utils/spendingComparison.ts`** (new, pure): `withPriorPeriod(report, priorReport)` attaches a same-period `priorYtd` to every row by summing the prior report's cells over the current year's month window (matched by id, `(No category)` by name); `spendingChange()` computes Δ/%/direction; `hasPriorData()` gates the toggle.
- **Toggle** — a `Compare {priorYear}` button next to Table|Chart. It's **always present but `disabled` when the prior year has no data** (with an explanatory tooltip). Effective state is `comparing = compare && hasPrior`, so stepping onto a year whose predecessor is empty silently disables it and re-enables on return.
- **Table** — two columns fold into the existing `valueCells` snippet (so every row type gets them): a muted **Prior-YTD** and a coloured **Change** (red = spent more, green = spent less, with signed amount + %, "new" when there's no prior spend). A caption states the compared window.
- **Chart** — `SpendingChart` gains a `compare` prop and draws a **dashed prior-period line** across each bar from the y-scale, plus prior/change rows in the hover tooltip.
- Data loading fetches the prior year alongside the current, so toggling repaints instantly with no refetch (the design's own "volume is negligible" argument).

## Verification
`npm run check` clean · ESLint + Prettier clean on touched files · new pure tests (`spendingComparison.spec.ts`, +2 in `spendingChart.spec.ts`) and +3 chart render tests all green · full suite green.

Two things to flag, both documented in the doc as known limitations (not bugs):
- **Disappeared spend is invisible in these two views** — a Grouping/Category that spent last year but nothing this year has no current row to annotate (the Grand Total still reflects it). Surfacing it needs the deferred diverging/waterfall views.
- **Marker overflow** — if a bar's prior total exceeds the tallest current bar, its dashed line sits above the plot; the tooltip always carries the exact number.

Per the repo's workflow rules I haven't committed or bumped `version.ts` — that's yours at commit time. As with the earlier slices, a rendered end-to-end pass needs your live check (no local auth/seed harness).

410	  partial in 2026 but was complete in 2025; the month-boundary rule compares
411	  Jan–Jul wholesale rather than clipping both to Jul 10. Simpler, matches the
412	  monthly grid, and is what the maintainer asked to start with. A day-boundary
413	  "pace" comparison is possible later (see the cumulative line below) but is not
414	  built.
415	
416	### The options (cheapest → richest)
417	
418	1. **YoY table columns** — after "Year to Date", a **Prior-YTD** column (same
419	   Jan→cutoff period, prior year) and a **Change** column (Δ amount + %). Same
420	   roll-up levels as today (category / group / importance / grand total). Pure
421	   extension of the aggregate; no new chart infra. **Built (below).**
422	2. **Prior-period marker on the magnitude bars** — a horizontal tick / ghost line
423	   at each bar's prior-YTD value; the gap between bar top and tick *is* the
424	   change, read in place with the accordion still working. **Built (below).**
425	3. **Cumulative "pace" line chart** — x = month (Jan → cutoff), y = running
426	   cumulative spend, **one line per year** overlaid, every line stopping at the
427	   same cutoff x so the parity rule is visually self-evident. The natural home
428	   for the month/time story deliberately dropped off the bars. **Deferred.**
429	4. **Diverging change bars** — one bar per Grouping = Δ vs prior YTD, increases
430	   one way / decreases the other, sorted by magnitude; best for *what* changed.
431	   **Deferred.** (Colour caution: the app already binds red = expense /
432	   green = refund, so a diverging chart must not reuse red/green for
433	   direction — use a neutral diverging pair or encode direction by side + sign.)
434	5. **Waterfall / bridge** — prior-YTD total → one ±step per Grouping →
435	   current-YTD total; decomposes the entire YoY change. Richest, least reuse.
436	   **Deferred.**
437	
438	Deliberately skipped: month×grouping heatmaps and indexed-to-100 growth curves —
439	legible only to spreadsheet-native users, and this report exists to *replace* the
440	family's manual pivot, not re-create its density.
441	
442	### What shipped (options 1 + 2, pending release)
443	
444	- **Toggle.** A **`Compare {priorYear}`** button in the header (next to
445	  Table | Chart) turns the comparison on/off for **both** views. When the prior
446	  year has **no data**, the toggle still renders but is **disabled** with an
447	  explanatory `title` ("No {priorYear} data to compare"). Effective state is
448	  `comparing = compare && hasPrior`, so stepping the year selector onto a year
449	  whose predecessor has no data silently disables it and re-enables on return.
450	  Comparison is **local page state** (like the Table | Chart toggle), not URL —
451	  it doesn't affect drill-down navigation, so it needn't survive Back.
452	- **Pure core.** `withPriorPeriod(report, priorReport)` in
453	  `src/lib/utils/spendingComparison.ts` attaches `priorYtd` (optional field added
454	  to `ReportRow`) to every row/subtotal/grand-total by summing the prior report's
455	  cells over the first `report.months.length` months (the parity window), matched
456	  by **id** (categoryId / groupId / importanceId) with `(No category)` matched by
457	  name. `spendingChange(current, prior) → { delta, pct, direction }` computes the
458	  Change cell (pct is `null` when prior is 0 → rendered "new"); `hasPriorData`
459	  gates the toggle. Both are unit-tested (`spendingComparison.spec.ts`).
460	- **Table.** The two columns fold into the existing `valueCells` snippet so every
461	  row type gets them; Prior-YTD is muted grey, Change is coloured **red = spent
462	  more / green = spent less / grey = flat** with a signed amount and %. The
463	  Importance/Uncategorized band `colspan`s widen by 2 when comparing.
464	- **Chart.** `buildSpendingChart` carries `priorTotal` onto each `ChartBar`
465	  (from the group/category `priorYtd`); `SpendingChart` (new `compare` prop) draws
466	  a dashed prior-period line across each bar from the bound y-scale, and adds the
467	  prior total + change to the hover tooltip. Data loading fetches the prior year's
468	  expenses alongside the current year's (volume is negligible per the aggregate's
469	  own design note), so switching the toggle repaints instantly with no refetch.
